title: Dissent to win
heading: Dissent to win
coreClaim: The chapter argues that groups improve decision quality when they reward dissent that surfaces evidence, assumptions, and disagreement honestly instead of smoothing everything into consensus.
distinctMechanism: Productive dissent raises truth-seeking quality by separating evidence conflict from ego conflict and by resisting consensus pressure.
requiredAnchors: Dissent as a truth-seeking group tool.
Consensus pressure as a decision risk.
The difference between useful challenge and conflict theater.
commonMisreadings: The chapter glorifies conflict for its own sake.
Any loud disagreement counts as valuable dissent.
specificApplications: Invite counterarguments before group decisions finalize.
Use disagreement to test assumptions and evidence quality.
Build norms that protect challenge without glamorizing hostility.
hardEdgeRequirement: Preserve the tension between real challenge and stable group function.
thresholdQuestion: How do groups create disagreement that improves truth rather than status games?
